officialHistory.finding: The camp began in the unfinished Ila women's prison and expanded from 1942 into a barracks camp of more than thirty buildings around the original prison complex. Nearly 20,000 people were registered during the occupation.

museumScope.finding: The current museum is located in an authentic prisoner barrack. MiA states that the barrack was moved back to Grini and stands just outside the original camp location. It is therefore a visitor anchor, not a centroid for the wartime camp.

historicalEntityCandidate.finding: Wikidata publishes a coordinate for the historical camp, but the statement has no cited coordinate reference and no documented derivation from the camp layout. It remains a candidate only.

legacyCoordinate.finding: The current marker lies east of the museum and the Wikidata historical point. It has no source object or documented relationship to the prison building, barracks camp, parade ground or preserved remains.

rejectedCandidate.finding: An OSM-derived index labels a farm/locality point as Grini detention camp. The object class and location are inconsistent with the documented Ila/Grini camp and museum area and are rejected.

historicalMapContext.sourceName: Bærumhistorie – Grini fangeleir and current-area map
historicalMapContext.finding: A wartime camp diagram and current topographic comparison show that the historical site was a broad compound containing the main prison building, parade ground, barracks, workshops, farms and perimeter functions. The images are useful for scope analysis but are not georeferenced production geometry.

decision.nextAction: Acquire or georeference an authoritative camp plan against the current Ila site, identify the main prison/parade-ground core and surviving original elements, then select a historical area anchor and separate museum visitor anchor.
